title: Case-insensitive filesystem paths can be registered twice with different casing (Parse Error: Class "XYZ" hides a global script class)
body:
### Tested versions

Godot 4.7
(i think this bug is there for long time.)

### System information

Windows 11

### Issue description

Case handling causes the same script to be registered twice on case-insensitive filesystems

There appears to be a bug in path case handling on case-insensitive operating systems such as Windows.

The same path can be processed internally with different casing, for example:

```text
res://Scripts/Main/Player.gd
res://scripts/main/Player.gd
```

These are the same file on a case-insensitive filesystem, but Godot appears to keep both path variants internally. This can cause the same script to be registered twice.

The resulting error is misleading:

```text
Parse Error: Class "XYZ" hides a global script class.
```

There is no duplicate class or duplicate script in the project. The same script is simply being registered more than once because its path exists internally with different casing.

The actual path may be:

```text
res://Scripts/Main/
```

while Godot reports or internally uses:

```text
res://scripts/main/
```

I suspect that some internal path lookup uses lowercase normalization, while other parts retain the original casing. This can cause both variants to end up in the same registry/hash table/dictionary.

On case-insensitive filesystems, paths should use a single canonical form for internal comparisons and registry keys. The original casing should still be preserved for display and project files, so users can choose their preferred path casing.

This issue can persist and repeatedly return in an affected project, making the misleading global-class error particularly difficult to resolve.

#### Solution

Simply normalizing hash table keys to lowercase internally causes problems on case-sensitive operating systems. I recommend path normalization that uses the actual, correctly cased path that physically exists on the filesystem and corrects the casing when necessary. This would solve all of these problems across all operating systems without requiring special handling for case-sensitive operating systems.


### Steps to reproduce


(in Minimal reproduction project)

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)


[CaseBug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32056867/CaseBug.zip)

This in CaseTest.tscn cause it.
But it can also happen that in a complex project, the error is reported in lowercase, even though the path is correctly cased in the '.tscn'. I was not able to reproduce where this originates.
